title: Hypothyroidism care through your AI: labs, medicine and a doctor by message
summary: This thyroid doctor online guide covers hypothyroidism treatment, TSH labs, levothyroxine, and Paloma Health vs FutureClinic's $40 visit by message.
body_markdown:
Managing hypothyroidism by message starts with ordering thyroid blood tests and adjusting levothyroxine without sitting in a waiting room. On FutureClinic, you message a licensed physician from your AI app or browser who can review TSH and free T4 labs, adjust your thyroid hormone dose, and send prescriptions to the pharmacy you choose.


A specific state-licensed doctor reads your history, lab numbers, and questions before writing back a medical plan with a Human Signature, a short video or voice note recorded live for you. No form is approved in bulk. Replies typically arrive within a few hours, and almost always the same day or the next, because real care takes hours rather than seconds. You can message the same doctor time after time in the same chat, however long in between, to track progress and adjust treatment together: comparing this month's TSH against last year's, stepping a dose up or down, rechecking labs after a generic switch, or raising your dose in pregnancy.


Your doctor can also help with other problems in their specialty, and when you see other specialists on FutureClinic, every FutureClinic doctor you see works from[one medical record](https://futureclinic.com/blog/one-online-doctor-for-everything-vs-condition-apps) so different kinds of care sit in one place. We believe AI is a tool for doctors and the doctor is in charge of every case, because only an expert knows when an AI makes a mistake. FutureClinic's AI works behind the scenes like a chief resident, gathering history and organizing your case without ever giving medical advice by itself.


## How do doctors diagnose and monitor hypothyroidism by message?


Per the[NIDDK](https://www.niddk.nih.gov/health-information/endocrine-diseases/hypothyroidism) , hypothyroidism means an underactive thyroid slows how the body uses energy. Nearly 5 in 100 Americans aged 12 and older have it; women are much more likely than men to get it, it is more common after age 60, and autoimmune Hashimoto's disease is the top cause. The[American Thyroid Association (ATA)](https://www.thyroid.org/hypothyroidism/) calls a blood test "the only way to know for sure". By message, a FutureClinic doctor orders discounted lab tests locally. Per the[USPSTF](https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/thyroid-dysfunction-screening) , TSH has about 98% sensitivity and 92% specificity in referred patients (normal about 0.4 to 4.5 mIU/L), while free T4 separates subclinical from overt disease. Stop biotin 2 to 3 days before testing.


### When does a mildly raised TSH need treatment?


In US survey data cited by the USPSTF, overt hypothyroidism affects about 3 per 1,000 people and subclinical disease (high TSH, normal free T4) about 46 per 1,000. Mild subclinical rises are retested over 3 to 6 months: TSH varies up to 50% daily, about 37% normalize untreated over several years, and the[2026 ATA pregnancy guidelines](https://escholarship.org/uc/item/0pw091c0) note up to 80% of mild rises in older adults normalize on repeat testing. Treatment generally starts above 10.0 mIU/L. In the[2017 TRUST trial](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28402245/) (737 older adults), levothyroxine lowered average TSH to 3.63 versus 5.48 mIU/L on placebo at one year without improving symptom or tiredness scores, matching a[2018 JAMA meta-analysis](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30285179/) and[2019 BMJ guideline](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31088853/) .


## AI hypothyroidism treatment: how levothyroxine and dose changes work


If your doctor decides it's right for you, standard treatment is levothyroxine, synthetic T4 recommended as the preparation of choice in the[2014 ATA guidelines](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4267409/) . Because it has a narrow therapeutic index, dosing is adjusted carefully; a TSH below 0.1 mIU/L raises atrial fibrillation and osteoporosis risks in older adults and postmenopausal women, while undertreatment harms lipids. On the[Synthroid label](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?labeltype=all&query=levothyroxine) , full replacement averages 1.6 mcg per kg daily (100 to 125 mcg for a 70 kg adult), adjusted by 12.5 to 25 mcg; the 2014 ATA guideline says milder cases need lower starting doses, such as 25 to 50 mcg, and the labels start older adults and people with heart disease at 12.5 to 25 mcg. Doctors recheck TSH 6 to 8 weeks after dose changes (4 to 6 weeks per ATA), after product switches, and every 6 to 12 months once stable.


Take levothyroxine fasting 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast or at bedtime 3+ hours after dinner ([ATA treatment guide](https://www.thyroid.org/thyroid-hormone-treatment/) ), separated by 4 hours from calcium or iron; coffee, soy, fiber, walnuts, and grapefruit juice reduce absorption. Porcine extracts like[Armour Thyroid](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?labeltype=all&query=thyroid) are FDA-unapproved on DailyMed, vary by batch, and can push T3 high, and a[2021 consensus](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33276704/) found 14 trials of levothyroxine plus[liothyronine](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?labeltype=all&query=liothyronine) showed no consistent benefit. In pregnancy, the[2026 ATA guidelines](https://escholarship.org/uc/item/0pw091c0) advise levothyroxine alone (often raised about 25% on a positive test, checking TSH every 4 weeks through mid-pregnancy), never T3 or extracts. A boxed warning states thyroid hormones are not for weight loss with normal thyroid function.
